key_insight: Combining clinical and genomic data modestly improved machine learning prediction of progression-free survival in HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer compared with single-modality models.
clinical_relevance: The model identified distinct prognostic risk groups and biological features for further study, but does not establish which treatment an individual should receive.
method: Integrated baseline clinical data, plasma ctDNA, and archival tumor gene expression from MONALEESA-2, -3, and -7.
Trained multimodal fusion models on 1,355 patients to predict progression-free survival.
Evaluated prognostic performance in 382 test-set patients using Kaplan–Meier, Cox, and Weibull analyses.
evidence_signal: Late fusion achieved a test-set C-index of 0.727 (95% CI, 0.641–0.799), versus 0.718 for early fusion, and separated low- from high-risk groups (PFS hazard ratio, 0.28; 95% CI, 0.20–0.38).
watch_item: External validation beyond MONALEESA trial populations is needed before routine clinical use; the small performance difference between fusion approaches has overlapping confidence intervals.
paper_title: Multimodal Machine Learning-Based Clinical and Genomic Prognostic Factors for Progression-Free Survival in Metastatic Breast Cancer Using Phase III MONALEESA Trials
